problem: Pre-trained perception models (grounding, segmentation, 3D box) degrade in embodied indoor scenes, and the usual fix of fine-tuning causes catastrophic forgetting and needs costly annotations. Prior active perception methods are coupled to specific models, closed-set tasks or need labeled data for retraining.
motivation: Perception quality depends on the informativeness of the viewpoint as well as on model capacity, so choosing better views can recover domain-gap losses without touching the perception models. A plug-and-play, label-free controller that works with language-specified targets would let off-the-shelf perception be used in open-world embodied settings.
key_idea: Freeze all perception modules and train a VLM as a low-level camera pose controller, first by SFT on heuristic exploration trajectories and then by GRPO with unsupervised rewards built from the frozen modules' confidence and geometric outputs.
insight: Neither stage alone works. RL-only training collapses, dropping VG mAP_avg by 39.90% relative to the pretrained module, and SFT-only gives modest gains (+4.10%), while SFT+RL gives +10.56% for the InternVL3.5-2B policy. In the reward ablation, confidence alone is noisy and hurts grounding and segmentation, and geometric alone is stable but limited. Combining them gives large, uniform gains. Oracle shortest-path navigation gives only modest gains, which shows that reaching the target is not the same as choosing a good viewpoint.
method: Problem formulation: an agent with a language instruction I and RGB observations controls the camera over at most T=10 steps to maximise the quality of frozen perception outputs, using only scalar feedback and no perceptual labels.
VLM policy: the VLM outputs structured thoughts, task type (routes to a perception module), task prompt, and one discrete action (move forward 0.25m, turn left/right 10°, look up/down, stop).
Frozen perception modules: GroundingDINO for VG, GroundingDINO+SAM for segmentation, mask+depth point cloud with min-area oriented 3D box fitting for 3D; each returns a prediction and a confidence.

SFT stage: a deterministic heuristic (rotate to search, center the target in a 3x3 grid, move forward until the area is large enough, then stop) generates trajectories with thoughts and actions for a cold start.

GRPO stage: reward = format (±0.05) + λ1·confidence delta between consecutive steps + λ2·geometric delta (area ratio and center alignment), with a -1 penalty for wrong task type. λ1=0.5, lr 1e-6, 4 rollouts, batch 8, KL 0.04, temperature 0.4.
Instruction synthesis: Qwen2.5-VL-7B generates open-vocabulary descriptions of a visible target object, which are wrapped in a task template such as 'segment the [p_I]'.

setting.backbone: Qwen3VL-2B and InternVL3.5-2B (fine-tuned by SFT then GRPO) as the policy; frozen GroundingDINO, SAM and a 3D box estimator as perception modules
setting.training_data: Rule-based heuristic trajectories (SFT) plus GRPO rollouts in 10 training scenes each of ReplicaCAD and HM3D; no perceptual labels; instructions generated by Qwen2.5-VL-7B
setting.observation: monocular RGB 512x512 at 1 m height; depth is used only by the 3D module, not by the policy
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: move forward 0.25 m, turn left/right 10°, look up/down 10°, stop; horizon T=10
setting.privileged: The ground-truth task type is used in the reward during training; the baselines Shortest Path (GT object positions), Heuristic, Forward and Random are given GT task type and target description; the policy itself uses none at test time.

numbers.eval_set_note: 500 tasks sampled from the 10 training scenes of ReplicaCAD (same scenes used for training)
numbers.extra: Frozen GroundingDINO/SAM/3D estimator; T=10 steps; test tasks come from the training scenes

numbers.eval_set_note: 500 tasks sampled from 10 training scenes of ReplicaCAD
500 tasks sampled from 10 training scenes of HM3D
500 tasks sampled from 10 training scenes of HM3D

numbers_note: This is not a standard navigation benchmark. Test tasks are drawn from the same 10 scenes used for training, so there is no unseen-scene split. The metrics are perception metrics, not SR/SPL.
results: Sea² with a Qwen3VL-2B policy improves the frozen pretrained perception on ReplicaCAD by +13.54% VG mAP_avg, +15.92% segmentation IoU and +27.68% 3D IoU. On HM3D the gains are +22.16%, +12.49% and +9.31%. It beats the oracle Shortest Path baseline (e.g. 0.8052 vs 0.7933 mAP_avg on ReplicaCAD) and the Forward, Random and Heuristic baselines, and untrained prompted VLMs fall below the static first-frame baseline.
limitations: Evaluation uses test tasks from the same 10 scenes the policy was trained on, so generalization to unseen scenes is not shown.
Only a discrete action set, 2B-scale VLMs and three GroundingDINO/SAM-based modules are tested, with no real-robot experiments.
Training rewards use the ground-truth task type, and correct task-type identification is required for a nonzero score.
